# C1. The path in levels {#esc-paths}

The calibration targets the design of 2020 only; every other design along the path is an outcome of the model,
chosen one period ahead. The first two figures follow the three countries from 1990, whose electorate sets the design
of 2020, to 2110; the demography is constant from 2080. Each country keeps its own calibration and demography. Its
cost parameter is either the U.S. λ, the deep test of [C7](esc-countries.qmd) along the path, or its own, the
parameter at which its electorate re-elects its observed design.

## By country {#esc-paths-countries}

In every country the chosen design moves against the number of workers per retiree. As the population ages, the
electorate ties benefits more closely to earnings, and the design levels off when the demography does. Under the
U.S. cost parameter the three countries' designs keep their observed order from 2020 on: the UK's lowest, France's
highest, the U.S. in between. France's design stays above the U.S. one, but from 2050 by much less, since France's
population is already old in 2020 and ages least afterwards. The UK's workers per retiree rise until 2020 before they
fall, and its design moves against them, falling and then rising. At their own parameters the UK's and France's
designs pass through their observed values in 2020 and follow the same patterns. The tax rate rises with ageing
everywhere.

::: {.oa-explorer .column-page}
{{< include _generated/exhibits/ESC_PathsCountries-head.qmd >}}

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
import {pathGrid, control, checkboxes, COUNTRIES, countryStyle, OUTCOMES} from "./assets/oa.js"
escPaths = FileAttachment("_generated/data/ESC_Paths.csv").csv({typed: true})
PATHVARS = [["Pension design θ", "theta"], ["Tax rate", "tau"], ["Savings over GDP", "sr"], ["Workweek", "workweek"]]
COSTS = [["the U.S. one for all", "US"], ["each country's own", "own"]]
NAME = ({US: "U.S.", UK: "UK", FR: "France"})
// One country's baseline path at rho = 1 under the paper's cost and the selected parameter, the U.S. one or its own.
countryPath = (country, cost) => escPaths.filter(d => (d.source === "main" || d.source === "host")
  && d.country === country && d.spec === "size" && d.rho === 1 && d.wedgeFrom === cost)
series = (rows, variable, reading) => rows.filter(d => d.variable === variable)
  .map(d => ({year: d.year, value: d[reading]})).sort((a, b) => a.year - b.year)
viewof c1Countries = checkboxes(COUNTRIES, {key: "countries", label: "Countries"})
viewof c1Var = control("select", PATHVARS, {key: "variable", label: "Beside workers per retiree", value: "theta"})
viewof c1Cost = control("radio", COSTS, {key: "cost", label: "Cost parameter", value: "US"})
{
  const lines = v => c1Countries.map(c => {
    const st = countryStyle(c);
    return {label: NAME[c], colour: st.colour, symbol: st.symbol,
            records: series(countryPath(c, c1Cost), v, v === "nu" ? "pinned" : "chosen")};
  });
  const observed = c1Var === "theta" ? c1Countries.map(c => {
    const r = countryPath(c, c1Cost).find(d => d.variable === "theta" && d.year === 2020);
    return r ? {year: 2020, value: r.pinned, colour: countryStyle(c).colour, text: `${NAME[c]}, observed design: ${r.pinned.toFixed(3)}`} : null;
  }).filter(d => d) : [];
  const items = c1Countries.map(c => ({label: NAME[c], colour: countryStyle(c).colour, shape: "line"}));
  if (observed.length) items.push({label: "observed design", colour: "#52514e", shape: "open"});
  return pathGrid([{title: "Workers per retiree ν", variable: "nu", lines: lines("nu"), rule: 2020, ruleLabel: "calibration"},
                   {title: OUTCOMES[c1Var].level, variable: c1Var, lines: lines(c1Var), rule: 2020,
                    ruleLabel: "calibration", observed}],
                  items, {width});
}
```

{{< include _generated/exhibits/ESC_PathsCountries-foot.qmd >}}
:::

## The design chosen and the design pinned {#esc-paths-readings}

With the design pinned at its observed value, each country's path is that of section {{< var p.sec_oecd >}} with the
cost in place. After 2020 the tax rate with the design chosen lies above the pinned path in every country and under
either parameter, consistent with the hump of [C3](esc-costs.qmd#esc-costs-pinned): at a given demography the tax
rate peaks close to the design the electorate chooses, so a design pinned away from that choice, on either side,
carries a lower one. At each country's own parameter, the U.S. included, the chosen design rises above the observed
one after 2020 as the population ages, and the tax rate lies only slightly above the pinned path. Under the U.S.
parameter the UK's chosen design lies above its observed one throughout and France's below it, and the gap in the tax
rate is largest in the UK.

::: {.oa-explorer .column-page}
{{< include _generated/exhibits/ESC_PathsReadings-head.qmd >}}

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof c1bCountry = control("radio", COUNTRIES, {key: "country", label: "Country", value: "US"})
viewof c1bVar = control("select", PATHVARS, {key: "variable2", label: "Beside workers per retiree", value: "theta"})
viewof c1bCost = control("radio", COSTS, {key: "cost2", label: "Cost parameter", value: "US"})
{
  const rows = countryPath(c1bCountry, c1bCost);
  const st = countryStyle(c1bCountry);
  const both = v => [
    {label: NAME[c1bCountry] + ", design chosen", colour: st.colour, symbol: st.symbol,
     records: series(rows, v, "chosen")},
    {label: NAME[c1bCountry] + ", design pinned", colour: st.colour, symbol: st.symbol, dashed: true,
     records: series(rows, v, "pinned")}];
  const items = [{label: "design chosen", colour: st.colour, shape: "line"},
                 {label: "design pinned at the observed value", colour: st.colour, shape: "line", dashed: true}];
  return pathGrid([{title: "Workers per retiree ν", variable: "nu", rule: 2020, ruleLabel: "calibration",
                    lines: [{label: NAME[c1bCountry], colour: st.colour, symbol: st.symbol, records: series(rows, "nu", "chosen")}]},
                   {title: OUTCOMES[c1bVar].level, variable: c1bVar, lines: both(c1bVar), rule: 2020, ruleLabel: "calibration"}],
                  items, {width});
}
```

## The U.S. path from the calibration year {#esc-paths-us}

The figure follows the U.S. from 2020, the calibration year, along its projected demography under log preferences,
with the design chosen and with it pinned at its observed value: the U.S. path of the figures above, drawn beyond 2110.
Since the calibration targets only the design of 2020, the path after 2020 is a prediction. The chosen design rises as
the number of workers per retiree falls, most between 2020 and 2050, and settles one period after the demography does.
The tax rate climbs with ageing and lies slightly above the path with the design pinned, since a more earnings-related
system loses less of its revenue. [C4](esc-parameters.qmd#esc-paths-parameters) shows the path at the other values of
the IES.
